decision_log.decision: Internal ZB Automations product, not a client. Money gates D/H/I do not apply (no deposit, no client invoice). Zach commissioned the first MVP from Manus and told the agent to proceed with the build framework.
Service type 'ios-game' and tier 'internal' are outside the schema v1 enums on purpose: no client service or price exists. funnel doctor will flag this; it is expected.
Private GitHub repo. Apple Developer Program to be bought when needed, not now. Bundle ID ie.zbautomations.pistonforge confirmed. Game is fully free for now.
Restart Piston Forge through the full funnel: planning, preview, approve, build, test, fix, publish, monitor, improve. Delete what Manus built.

Moved Phase F back to Phase E (WAITING_FOR_DESIGN_APPROVAL). Deleted the Manus preview tooling folders and build hook. Kept the Manus-generated game code (src/sim, src/game, src/audio, src/ui) on the advisor's recommendation until Zach approves the per-part keep/rewrite list in docs/plan/phase-e-plan.md. Stage stays building: the enum has no planning value for an internal product.
Approved the per-part keep/rewrite list (phase-e-plan section 1) and the v1 cut list (section 4: handling lap cut).
Piston Forge is iOS only, forever. Build natively in Swift using the Apple iOS skills; no web code, no Capacitor.
Dark only, but not black: dark grey with game-colour hues in the background.
Preview widths: 430 px phone and 1032 px iPad plus landscape phone.

Reading of the Swift decision against the approved keep list: the TypeScript code is not kept; the simulation MODEL (formulas, constants, behaviour) is ported to Swift and checked against golden fixtures exported from the TS sim. Career and interface are redesigned as planned. 3D in RealityKit (SceneKit is deprecated for new apps since WWDC 2025). TS/Capacitor code stays until the Swift sim passes the fixtures. Gate E still not passed: design approval is separate.
Start over: the Swift version is a fresh design, not a port. Plan with planning skills, subagents and the advisor; build with the Swift skills; test; deliver an .ipa.

Game concept: an engine tuning simulator. App opens on a fully assembled engine with all connections hooked up. Layouts I3, I4, V6, V8, V10, V12, W16; 60 and 90 degree V angles; flat-plane and cross-plane cranks; NA, turbo, supercharger; big injectors, nitrous; sensors (MAF, injector and others). Dyno to test, modify and upgrade. Then put the engine in a car and drive it.

Driving v1: a flat open proving ground (grid-map style, our own design) with a straight, corners, skidpads and a chase camera, plus a drag strip with quarter, half and full mile variants, markers at each and distance markers the whole way up. This reverses the earlier cut of the handling lap.
Car feel: proper simulation (tyre grip and slip, weight transfer, wheelspin, clutch and gears), not arcade.

No career, money or unlocks in v1: a pure tuning sandbox, everything open. Build order: (1) engine view + parts + dyno + engine sound, (2) drag strip, (3) proving ground. Each stage ends with an .ipa on his phone.
Stage 1 ships everything at once: all layouts incl. W16, all induction types, nitrous, full sensor set. Engine sound plays with the ringer switch on silent.
"design approved": approved docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-16-piston-forge-native-design.md. Simulation and physics code may start; each stage's screen code waits for its previews to be approved.

Agent's reading of Zach's answers (1: 'your recommendation', 2: 'yes', 4: 'yes add inline six'): execute the stage 1 plan; main session writes the Swift, Haiku subagents review each task, advisor at key points.
Changelog rule change approved: compile-fix commits on the same plan task share (amend) that task's changelog entry.
Add an inline six (I6) to the stage 1 layouts.
